piece.name: Still Seeking
piece.title: Still Seeking (FormaComposition) v1
piece.notes: Eliminator-model rock: bass_style pulse gives the sequenced-synth 'platform' (deliberately low, out of the riff's register); voices[0]='riff' motif (develop) rides on top. Harmony strikes on the riff's own rhythm (harmony_rhythm.rhythm=motif) for Ob-La-Di-style chord stabs rather than sustained pads. Mixolydian's native VII is already flat -- written bare as 'VII', NOT 'bVII' (bVII would double-flatten it against the major-scale reference -- see harmony.py's _roman_degree_to_root_midi docstring). Progression I-VII-IV throughout is the AC/DC/mixolydian skeleton. No power-chord (root+fifth, no third) voicing exists in this engine's chord-quality system -- density:'sparse' (triad only) is the closest available, flagged as a known gap, not silently worked around.

intro.notes: Pulse and drums establish the platform first, riff not in yet -- mirrors Eliminator's build order: rhythm section programmed before the guitar layers in.

verse_1.notes: Riff locked in via voices[0], develop behavior (the only one that reads motif pitch). Chord stabs ride the riff's own rhythm cell. Bass stays low and out of the riff's register, per Gibbons' platform principle.

chorus.notes: Lift to IV, fuller chord density for the hook. This single definition is reused for both choruses via exact_repeat -- the hook stays identical each time it lands.

verse_2.notes: Same feel as verse_1; independent section name (not exact_repeat) so it can carry its own seed-derived variation.

break.notes: Static pedal on I -- this is the solo pocket. Chord chart holds one chord the whole section so guitar has open space; riff voice uses 'develop' here (not exact_repeat) to genuinely vary rather than lock.

chorus_final.notes: Peak intensity -- full chord density, hottest velocity. Intentionally NOT a repeat of chorus, same pattern as shake_v5's chorus_final.

outro.notes: Riff drops out, pulse settles to a pedal, drums thin -- mirrors the intro build in reverse.
